## Overview

The same machinery applies within a host. In the basic model of viral dynamics (Perelson
and Nelson 1999), target cells `T` are produced at rate `s` and die at rate `d`, free
virions `V` infect target cells at rate `β`, infected cells `I` die at rate `δ` and produce
virions at rate `p`, and virions are cleared at rate `c`. Both `I` and `V` are "infected"
states, and the choice of which events count as reproduction is exactly the vector–host
question of vignette 4: counting both cell infection and virion production gives
`R₀ = √(p β T₀ / (c δ))`, counting only cell infection gives the familiar
`R₀ = p β T₀ / (c δ)`.

## The model

```{julia}
using ReproductiveNumbers, Catalyst, ModelingToolkit, Symbolics

vd = @reaction_network viral_dynamics begin
    @parameters s d β δ p c
    s, 0 --> T
    d, T --> 0
    β, T + V --> I + V
    δ, I --> 0
    p, I --> I + V
    c, V --> 0
end
@unpack T, I, V, s, d, β, δ, p, c = vd
```

The infection-free steady state has `T₀ = s/d` and is found automatically:

```{julia}
disease_free_equilibrium(vd, [I, V])
```

## Two generations per cycle

By the stoichiometry rule both `T + V --> I + V` (a new infected cell) and `I --> I + V`
(a new virion) are transmissions:

```{julia}
ngm = next_generation_matrix(vd, [I, V])
```

```{julia}
basic_reproduction_number(ngm)
```

## One generation per cycle

Counting only the infection of cells as reproduction, virion production is a transition:

```{julia}
ngm_cells = next_generation_matrix(vd, [I, V]; transmission = rx -> any(isequal(I), rx.products) && any(isequal(T), rx.substrates))
states_at_infection(ngm_cells), basic_reproduction_number(ngm_cells)
```

The two conventions give `R₀` and `R₀²`; both have the same threshold. The mean sojourn
times explain the second form: an infected cell "spends" `p/(δ c)` virion-lifetimes
producing virus.

```{julia}
mean_sojourn_times(ngm_cells)
```

## Numbers

```{julia}
vals = Dict(s => 1e4, d => 0.01, β => 2e-7, δ => 0.5, p => 100.0, c => 5.0)
(basic_reproduction_number(ngm, vals), basic_reproduction_number(ngm_cells, vals))
```
